title: Encode and Decode Strings
description: Encode each string as its decimal length, a # separator, and its contents. Decode by reading each length and consuming exactly that many characters.
note: A separator inside a string is ordinary content. Length prefixes preserve empty strings and avoid escaping or splitting the payload.
notes: The encoding of ["bird", "", "a#b"] is "4#bird0#3#a#b". An empty list encodes as "", while one empty string encodes as "0#".
str(word.size) formats the length as decimal text. parts.extend collects string fragments, and parts.join("") combines them once without changing the list or repeatedly copying a growing result.

The decoder scans to the header separator, parses its decimal length with int, then extracts data[start:cursor]. The slice excludes cursor and returns a str, while data[separator] returns a char compared with '#'.
String sizes, indices, and slice boundaries all count Unicode scalar values. The encoder and decoder therefore agree for non-ASCII text too, without normalization or a byte-length convention.

Both functions are stateless and can be top-level helpers. The Python judge wrapper only groups them. The decoder assumes data was produced by encode; validating arbitrary malformed input is outside this example.

For n input strings containing T total Unicode scalar values, each function takes O(T + n) time and O(T + n) space including its output, under ordinary integer/index cost assumptions. This includes length headers, empty strings, and any one-time linear preparation for scalar indexing; repeated indexing must not rescan the string prefix.
